title: Hornbeam: Ancient Hornbeams You Can Visit
meta_description: A hedge species left free to grow: a 19-metre giant in Aarhus, a Copenhagen tree stripped of pacifiers each November, a Nijmegen elder by a sequoia.
intro: Carpinus betulus is Europe's shear-proof hedge tree, planted by the thousand for its density and its patience under a blade, which is why a hornbeam left alone to grow into its full, fluted-trunked shape reads as a surprise. Salzburg's, outside the old biology institute on Freisaalweg, is put at more than 200 years and carries a strikingly round, globe-shaped crown on several stems. York's cut-leaved hornbeam is hollow and curls into itself, its canopy low enough to brush the grass. Copenhagen's in Frederiksberg Have is the Pacifier Tree, harvested bare every November of the dummies local toddlers tie to it. And Enschede shows what the hedge habit can do at scale: the Beukenberceau of Van Heekpark, the beech arbour, is about a hundred hornbeams clipped into a green tunnel for about a century, and contains no beech at all.
